messages.message:
Patch Set 1:

(6 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. The removed check also caught max_brw == 0 and acted as the only bound on client-supplied nfrags before the bd_vec allocation, so removing it outright re-exposes both. Keeping a relaxed check (e.g. against LNET_MAX_IOV * PTLRPC_BULK_OPS_COUNT, plus max_brw == 0) would fix the reconnect ENOMEM without that. A regression test would also help: lower obdfilter.*.brw_size, force a client reconnect with large dirty extents cached, and check the writes complete.

Patch Set 5:

(3 comments)

PS5 keeps the right direction: capacity checks in the frag helpers returning -EOVERFLOW instead of LASSERT, the max_brw==0 guard, and the nfrags bound on the server side are all fine. But the add_iov_frag() callers now break, because add_iov_frag() (ptlrpc_prep_bulk_frag_pages()) returns desc->bd_nob, a positive byte count, on success.

The two callers assign that to rc and return it, and their callers treat any non-zero rc as failure. batch_prep_update_req() then double-frees the batch head (the review-dne crash), and osp_prep_update_req() never sends non-inline updates and leaks the request. Details inline.

Patch Set 6:

(7 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Mostly good; the bulk-descriptor and caller error handling now look right. Patch set 6 added a separate obdfilter brw_size behaviour change. That change should be described in the commit message or moved to its own patch, see inline. The other inline items are optional for the next refresh.

Patch Set 5:

(3 comments)

Patch Set 6:

(2 comments)

Re-checked PS6 against PS5. The add_iov_frag() problem from my PS5 review is fixed: ptlrpc_prep_bulk_frag_pages() now returns 0 on success, and batch_prep_update_req() and osp_prep_update_req() check only rc < 0, so a non-inline batch or OUT update is sent again and its request is no longer freed twice or leaked. The other add_iov_frag() callers (mgc_target_register, mgc_nid_notify, mgs_target_reg, tgt_update_bufs_get) now check the result too, and the HPE-bug-id trailer is fixed.

The new brw_size check in lproc_ofd.c is correct and fixes a real problem. A brw_size that is not a power of two makes the client send an ioo_max_brw that tgt_io_data_unpack() rejects with -EPROTO, so the advice added by LU-20564 never worked. It is a separate, user-visible change though (see inline). I agree with the AI review that it needs its own paragraph in the commit message, or better its own patch.

One question inline about -EOVERFLOW on the batch path. With the current page_count slack I do not see it being reachable, so it does not block this patch. The code now addresses the older AI review threads (PS1 client.c, PS4 osp_trans.c and batch.c). Please reply to them and resolve them before landing.

Pre-existing, not touched by this patch: mdunlink_iterate_helper() is called with bd_md_max_brw. That value can be PTLRPC_BULK_OPS_COUNT (128), which mgs_target_reg() and tgt_update_bufs_get() pass in directly, but bd_mds[] has only PTLRPC_BULK_OPS_LIMIT (65) entries. So the abort and unregister paths read past the array. This is worth a separate ticket.

Tests and CI: PS6 still adds no regression test for the reconnect case. Build 137667 passed all 22 enforced Maloo sessions, and jenkins built it.

commit.subject: LU-20875 ptlrpc: let be less strict for max frags
commit.message:
LU-20875 ptlrpc: let be less strict for max frags

The server might reduce the maximum bulk size after the initial
connection, and this could cause large extents to be created
and prepared for sending. Therefore, it might exceed the current
limit. Let's make the bulk size checking less strict.

Instead of rejecting the whole bulk descriptor at creation time, do
the capacity check in the place which knows the real descriptor state.
add_kiov_frag() was declared void, so a fragment which does not fit
could only be reported with an LASSERT, and both limit checks were
done after the store, so an out of bounds write into bd_vec[] or
bd_mds_off[] happened before the panic.

Check the bd_max_iov and PTLRPC_BULK_OPS_LIMIT bounds before storing,
return -EOVERFLOW instead, and make every add_kiov_frag() caller fail
the RPC.

Fixes: e1ac9e74 ("LU-10157 ptlrpc: fill md correctly.")
